parts.article:
Insect-inspired robots
 
A recent conference reports on developments in biorobotics
 
A A tiny insect navigates its way across featureless salt-pans. A cockroach successfully works out how to scramble over an obstacle. The mantis shrimp scans its aquatic world through hyperspectral eyes. Using the most basic of equipment and brains tinier than a pin-head, insects constantly solve complex problems of movement, vision and navigation – processing data that would challenge a super-computer. How they do it is driving one of the most exciting new fields of technology – biomimetics and biorobotics, the imitation of insect systems to control man-made machines. Delegates at a recent conference presented some outcomes of their work in this area.
 
B Dr Alex Zelinsky suggested that the method by which wasps use landmarks to find their way back to the nest may one day be part of a system for navigating cars that know where to go. A research team led by Dr Zelinsky has shown that a robot can navigate its way among 50 different landmarks by recognising them individually using a panoramic camera. “The inspiration came from biology, where wasps use a practical method turn back and look to orient themselves as they emerge from their nest. By flying to and fro, they look at the wasp nest from different angles and perspectives so they can recognise it again,” he explained. The robot’s panoramic camera logs the surrounding area and its key landmarks, which are then stored in its computer according to how reliable they are as navigational aids. The landmarks are then scaled, from small to large, so that the robot can recognise whether it is getting closer to or further away from them. Their location is built into a map in its mind, which operates at different scales and instructs the robot whether to turn left or right at a particular mark. The technology provides a general way for a machine to navigate an unknown landscape.
 
C For three decades, Professor Ruediger Wehner has journeyed from Switzerland to the Sahara Desert where Cataglyphis, a tiny ant with a brain weighing just 0.1 mg, performs acts of navigational genius when it leaves its nest, forages for food and returns successfully. Cataglyphis uses polarised light, caused when air molecules scatter light, to orient and steer itself. Wehner’s team found that the ant has a set of specialised photoreceptors along the upper rim of its eyes that detect polarised light, while other receptors perform different navigational tasks. As the sun moves, the ant notes its direction each time it leaves the nest and updates its internal compass. Using other eye receptors it stores a snapshot image of landmarks close to the nest entrance in its eyes and compares this with what it sees as it returns. The ant also has a way of measuring distance travelled, while a path integrator periodically informs the ant of its current position relative to its point of departure. Rather than integrate all the information it receives in its brain, the ant actually performs a number of complex calculations in different organs. Like a super-computer, the ant has many separate sub-routines going on simultaneously. Using the ant’s ability to steer by polarised light and to store and reuse landscape images, Wehner and colleagues have built “Sahabot,” a small vehicle that uses polarisers and a CCD camera to store 360° images of its surroundings. It navigates by using polarised sunlight and comparing the current images of landmarks to the ones in its memory.
 
D Professor Robert Michelson had a different desert challenge – to design a flying robot that can not only navigate but also stay aloft and hover in the thin atmosphere of Mars. Drawing inspiration from insect flight, he has gone beyond nature to devise a completely new concept for a flying machine. The “Entomopter” is a sort of double-ended dragonfly whose wings beat reciprocally. Michelson says that the flapping-wing design gives the craft unusually high lift compared with a fixed-wing flyer, enabling it to fly slowly or hover in the thin Martian air – whereas a fixed-wing craft would have to move at more than 400 km/h and could not stop to explore.
 
E Engineer Roger Quinn and entomologist Professor Roy Ritzmann are taking their inspiration from cockroaches. According to Quinn and Ritzmann, the ability of cockroaches to run very fast over rough terrain may one day give rise to a completely new all-terrain vehicle with six legs, or maybe even wheel-like legs called “whegs.” The key to the cockroach’s remarkable cross-country performance lies partly in the fact that its legs do a lot of the thinking without having to consult the brain. Quinn and Ritzmann are drawing on cockroach skills to create robotic walkers and control strategies that capture the remarkable capacity of these insects to traverse complex terrain and navigate safely toward goals while avoiding obstacles. The team has already designed a series of robots that run on six legs or on whegs, enabling them to handle surprisingly rugged terrain.
 
F International experts believe there are tremendous opportunities in biorobotics. However, delegates at the conference had differing visions for the future of the science. While some were concerned that the initial applications of biorobotics may be military, others, such as Dr Barbara Webb, predicted swarms of tiny, cheap, insect-like robots as society’s cleaners and collectors. Sonja Kleinlogel hoped the study of the hyperspectral eyes of the mantis shrimp might yield remote sensors that can watch over the environmental health of our oceans. Several delegates were concerned about the ethical implications of biorobotics and urged that close attention be paid to this as the science and technologies develop.

questions.question: positive and negative possibilities for the use of insect-inspired robots

analyses.content: 不要看到“military”（军事）就觉得全是负面，或者只看到“cleaners”（清洁）觉得全是正面，这段话涵盖了正反两方面（positive and negative）。
(Section F) “While some were concerned that the initial applications of biorobotics may be military, others... predicted swarms of tiny, cheap, insect-like robots as society’s cleaners...”
F段讨论了仿生机器人的未来前景，既有积极的一面（如作为清洁工、环境监测），也有消极/令人担忧的一面（如军事用途、伦理问题），对应选项 F。

questions.question: how perceived size is used as an aid to navigation

analyses.content: B段提到机器人会将地标“从大到小缩放（scaled, from small to large）”，以此判断自己是在靠近还是远离目标，这正是利用感知到的大小来导航，对应选项 B。
题目中的“perceived size”在文中对应的就是“scaled... small to large”，不要因为没找到“size”这个词就略过。
(Section B) “The landmarks are then scaled, from small to large, so that the robot can recognise whether it is getting closer to or further away from them.”

questions.question: an example of decision-making taking place in the limbs

analyses.content: E段指出蟑螂的“腿（legs）”可以在不咨询大脑的情况下完成很多“思考（thinking）”，即肢体进行决策，对应选项 E。
看到“limbs”（肢体）要能联想到原文中的“legs”，并且抓住核心描述“legs do a lot of the thinking”。
(Section E) “...the key to the cockroach’s remarkable cross-country performance lies partly in the fact that its legs do a lot of the thinking without having to consult the brain.”

questions.question: a description of a potential aid in space exploration

analyses.content: (Section D) “...enabling it to fly slowly or hover in the thin Martian air – whereas a fixed-wing craft... could not stop to explore.”
D段描述了一种像蜻蜓一样的飞行机器人“Entomopter”，它能在火星（Mars）稀薄的大气中悬停和探索，属于太空探索辅助，对应选项 D。
C段提到的Sahara Desert（撒哈拉沙漠）是地球上的地方，只有D段的“Mars”（火星）才对应space exploration。

questions.question: the range of skills that have inspired biorobotics

analyses.content: A段作为开头，罗列了昆虫的多种技能（导航、翻越障碍、高光谱视觉等），展示了激发仿生机器人研究的广泛技能范围，对应选项 A。
这一段是总述（introduction），列举了movement, vision, navigation等多种能力，而不是只关注某一种。

(Section A) “A tiny insect navigates its way... A cockroach successfully works out how to scramble... The mantis shrimp scans its aquatic world... insects constantly solve complex problems of movement, vision and navigation...”

questions.question: how a variety of navigational methods operate at the same time

analyses.content: C段描述蚂蚁像超级计算机一样，同时（simultaneously）运行多个子程序（利用偏振光、地标图像、计步等），对应选项 C。
关键词是“at the same time”，对应文中的“simultaneously”，这表明多种机制是并行工作的。
(Section C) “...the ant actually performs a number of complex calculations in different organs... many separate sub-routines going on simultaneously.”

Reading Passage 3 has six sections, A-F.
Which section contains the following information?
Write the correct letter, A-F, in boxes 27–32 on your answer sheet.

groups.contentHtml:
Which creature sees particularly well under water?
In addition to a computer, what technical equipment is fitted in Dr Zelinsky’s robot?
Where is the Cataglyphis ant found?
What atmospheric effect helps the Cataglyphis ant to know its direction?

analyses.content: A段提到“mantis shrimp（螳螂虾）”通过高光谱眼睛扫描它的水下世界（aquatic world），说明它在水下视力极佳。
答案必须包含“mantis”，只写“shrimp”可能不够准确，因为原文特指这一物种。
(Section A) “The mantis shrimp scans its aquatic world through hyperspectral eyes.”
题目已经排除了computer，所以要在Dr Zelinsky的研究描述中寻找另一个核心硬件设备。
(Section B) “A research team led by Dr Zelinsky has shown that a robot can navigate its way... by recognising them individually using a panoramic camera.”
题目问除了电脑还有什么设备，B段提到该机器人使用“a panoramic camera（全景相机）”来识别地标。
题目问Cataglyphis蚂蚁在哪里被发现，C段开头明确提到教授前往“the Sahara Desert”研究这种蚂蚁。
不要误填“Switzerland”，那是教授出发的地方，不是蚂蚁的栖息地。
(Section C) “For three decades, Professor Ruediger Wehner has journeyed from Switzerland to the Sahara Desert where Cataglyphis... performs acts of navigational genius...”
题目问什么大气效应帮助蚂蚁辨别方向，原文说是“polarised light（偏振光）”，这是由空气分子散射光线产生的。
题目问的是帮助辨别方向的“效应/现象”，而不是问其成因（air molecules），所以填polarised light。
(Section C) “Cataglyphis uses polarised light, caused when air molecules scatter light, to orient and steer itself.”

analyses.content: (Section B) “...stored in its computer according to how reliable they are as navigational aids.”
B段提到Zelinsky的机器人将地标存储在电脑中，并根据它们“有多可靠（how reliable they are）”进行分类，对应选项 D（根据有用性分类信息）。
“Reliable”（可靠）对应选项中的“usefulness”（有用性），这是同义替换的核心。
C段提到Wehner团队制造了“Sahabot”，它利用“polarised sunlight”以及存储的“images”来导航，对应选项 A（利用光和存储图像）。
只要在C段找到Wehner的名字，然后锁定他发明的Sahabot利用了哪两种东西（光+图像）即可。
(Section C) “It navigates by using polarised sunlight and comparing the current images of landmarks to the ones in its memory.”
D段提到Michelson设计的“Entomopter”超越了自然（gone beyond nature），创造了全新的概念，提升了升力，对应选项 F（在昆虫能力基础上进行了改良）。
“Improved on the ability”对应原文的“gone beyond nature... unusually high lift”。
(Section D) “...he has gone beyond nature to devise a completely new concept for a flying machine... gives the craft unusually high lift compared with a fixed-wing flyer...”

questions.question: Roger Quinn and Professor Roy Ritzmann

analyses.content: E段提到这两位专家的灵感来自蟑螂，制造的机器人可以在“rough terrain（崎岖地形）”上跑得很快，对应选项 C（在困难表面移动）。
“Difficult surfaces”是“rough terrain”和“rugged terrain”的完美同义替换。
(Section E) “...create robotic walkers... to traverse complex terrain... enabling them to handle surprisingly rugged terrain.”
